# sanity_studio_deployment (Resource)

Deploys a pre-built Sanity Studio bundle to Sanity's hosted studio infrastructure. The studio will be available at `<hostname>.sanity.studio`. Build your studio with `sanity build` and provide the resulting tarball.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Deploy a pre-built studio bundle
#
# Build workflow:
#   cd studio
#   npm ci && npx sanity build
#   tar -czf ../studio.tar.gz -C dist .
#
resource "sanity_studio_deployment" "main" {
  project_id = sanity_project.blog.id
  hostname   = "my-company"

  bundle           = "${path.module}/studio.tar.gz"
  source_code_hash = filebase64sha256("${path.module}/studio.tar.gz")
}

# Deploy with auto-updates and explicit version
resource "sanity_studio_deployment" "staging" {
  project_id = sanity_project.blog.id
  hostname   = "my-company-staging"

  bundle           = "${path.module}/studio.tar.gz"
  source_code_hash = filebase64sha256("${path.module}/studio.tar.gz")

  auto_updates = true
  version      = "3.82.0"
}

# Use a data source to reference the deployed URL
output "studio_url" {
  value = sanity_studio_deployment.main.url
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bundle` (String) Path to the `.tar.gz` bundle of the built studio. Build with `sanity build` then `tar -czf studio.tar.gz -C dist .`.
- `hostname` (String) The hostname for the deployed studio. The studio will be available at `<hostname>.sanity.studio`.
- `project_id` (String) The project ID to deploy the studio for.

### Optional

- `auto_updates` (Boolean) Whether the studio should automatically update to the latest version. Defaults to `false`.
- `source_code_hash` (String) Hash of the bundle file used to trigger redeployment. Use `filebase64sha256()` on the bundle path.
- `version` (String) The Sanity package version string, e.g. `3.0.0`. Informational metadata sent with the deployment.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The user application ID.
- `url` (String) The URL of the deployed studio, e.g. `https://my-company.sanity.studio`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Import an existing studio deployment by project_id/hostname
terraform import sanity_studio_deployment.main abc123/my-company
```
